**@refoldai/refold-js**

***

# Refold Javascript SDK
Refold frontend SDK.

## Install

#### npm
```bash
npm install @refoldai/refold-js
```

#### yarn
```bash
yarn add @refoldai/refold-js
```

## Usage

### Include

#### Browser
```html
<!-- use this if you get an error saying `exports` is not defined. -->
<script>var exports = {};</script>
<!-- use a specific version -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@refoldai/refold-js@10.0.0"></script>
<!-- use a version range instead of a specific version -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@refoldai/refold-js@10"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@refoldai/refold-js@10.0"></script>
<!-- omit the version completely to use the latest one -->
<!-- you should NOT use this in production -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@refoldai/refold-js"></script>
```

#### Node
```js
import { Refold } from "@refoldai/refold-js";
// or, if you're using CommonJS
const { Refold } = require("@refoldai/refold-js");
```

### Initialize
```js
// initialize with the single-use code from the connect URL (recommended)
const refold = new Refold({
    // the code in the /connect/<code> URL you generated on your backend
    code: "REFOLD_CONNECT_CODE",
    // OPTIONAL: set custom base url for all API requests. only useful if you are hosting Refold on premise.
    baseUrl: "https://refold.example.com/backend",
});

// initialize with a session token
const refold = new Refold({
    // the token you generate for linked accounts using the Refold backend SDK
    token: "REFOLD_SESSION_TOKEN",
});

// initialize with a callback that fetches a token from your backend
const refold = new Refold({
    // called on start, shortly before the token expires, and when a request is rejected with 401
    getToken: async () => {
        // e.g. your backend calls Refold's session token endpoint for the signed-in customer
        const { token, expires_in } = await fetch("/api/refold-token", { method: "POST" }).then(res => res.json());
        return { access_token: token, expires_in };
    },
});

// Or, initialize without either
const refold = new Refold();
// and you can set the token later.
refold.token = "REFOLD_SESSION_TOKEN";
```

Prefer `code`. It is spent the first time the SDK uses it, so a connect URL that
reaches the wrong person is already worthless — a session token in the same place
stays usable until it expires. The SDK trades the code for a token as soon as it
is constructed and holds that token in memory only.

Create one instance per page load, in the browser, with a code minted on your
backend for that page load. Instances on the same page given the same code share
one exchange, but a reload, a second tab, or constructing the SDK during
server-side rendering each spends the code again — and a spent code is rejected.

Use `getToken` when a page can outlive its token: a token that expires or is revoked
mid-session otherwise fails every later call. Resolve `{ access_token, expires_in }`.
The SDK fetches a new token shortly before `expires_in` runs out, even on an idle page, and when a request
is rejected with 401 it fetches one and retries that request once. Tokens are held in
memory only. `getToken` supersedes `code`; with `token` also given, that token is used
first.

### ConnectorAuthType

Defined in: [refold.ts:17](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L17)

The auth types a universal connector can offer, as keyed in
[Application.auth\_type\_options](#auth_type_options). A native application is only ever an
[AuthType](#authtype); a connector names its own and may support several, so the caller has
to say which one it is submitting.

Returns the application details for the specified application, provided
the application is enabled in Refold. If no application is specified,
it returns all the enabled applications.

## Interfaces

### AccessToken

Defined in: [refold.ts:315](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L315)

What a [RefoldOptions.getToken](#gettoken) callback resolves to: the shape of an OAuth token response.

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description | Defined in |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
| <a id="access_token"></a> `access_token` | `string` | The token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. | [refold.ts:317](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L317) |
| <a id="expires_in"></a> `expires_in?` | `number` | How many seconds the token stays valid. Without it, the token is replaced only after a 401. | [refold.ts:319](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L319) |

### ConnectionScoped

Defined in: [refold.ts:229](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L229)

Names the connection a call acts on. An account holds one config per connection under
the same `config_id`, so `config_id` alone does not identify one. Omitted, the call
targets the default connection, which an application on auth profiles may not have —
writing a config for one without naming its connection is rejected.

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description | Defined in |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
| <a id="connectionid"></a> `connectionId?` | `string` | The unique ID of the connection, from [Application.connected\_accounts](#connected_accounts). | [refold.ts:231](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L231) |

| <a id="signal-1"></a> `signal?` | `AbortSignal` | Signal used to give up on an in-progress authentication — abort it and the returned promise resolves `false`. Providers that sever the authentication window's handle make an abandoned flow undetectable, so this is the only way to end such a wait before the `timeout`. | - | [refold.ts:196](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L196) |

### RefoldOptions

Defined in: [refold.ts:292](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L292)

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description | Defined in |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
| <a id="baseurl"></a> `baseUrl?` | `string` | The base URL of the Refold API. You don't need to set this. | [refold.ts:294](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L294) |
| <a id="code"></a> `code?` | `string` | The single-use code from a connect URL, traded for a session token as soon as the SDK is constructed. Instances on one page given the same code share that exchange. Prefer this over `token`: a code that reaches the wrong person is already spent, whereas a token stays usable until it expires. Ignored if `token` or `getToken` is also given. | [refold.ts:303](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L303) |
| <a id="gettoken"></a> `getToken?` | () => `Promise`\<[`AccessToken`](#accesstoken)\> | Fetches a token from your backend, for tokens that expire during a session. The SDK calls it when constructed, again shortly before the token's `expires_in` runs out (on a timer, so an idle page keeps a valid token), and again when a request is rejected with 401, which it then retries once. Tokens are held in memory only. With `token` also given, that token is used first and this is called only to replace it. | [refold.ts:311](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L311) |
| <a id="token-1"></a> `token?` | `string` | The session token. | [refold.ts:296](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L296) |

What kind of connector an application is. Universal connectors are configured in

### ExecutionType

> **ExecutionType** = `"SYNC"` \| `"ASYNC"`

Defined in: [refold.ts:396](https://github.com/gocobalt/refold-js/blob/2fbbacf1e01d9cada433a99e6acbe9d9fd12cda1/refold.ts#L396)

Whether a workflow execution runs synchronously (waits for result) or asynchronously (fire-and-forget).
